newsitem.title: USA: Applied Magnetics delays production ramp-up.
newsitem.headline: Applied Magnetics delays production ramp-up.

text.p: Applied Magnetics Corp, a maker of thin-film recording heads for the computer industry, Monday said it will delay a production ramp-up from fiscal 1997's fourth quarter into fiscal 1998's first quarter.
The company previously announced plans to double its production rates in the fourth quarter, but in a statement said lower production yields have caused the delay.

In addition, the company said gross margins in its recently completed third quarter of fiscal 1997 fell to 32.1 percent from 38.4 percent in the second quarter, but they were higher than the 24.2 percent in fiscal 1996's second quarter.

Applied Magnetics said fiscal fourth quarter gross margins "will depend heavily on the company's ability to increase yields on the 1.7-gigabyte-per3.5-inch disk products. The fourth quarter will be this product line's first of full production.

Earlier, Applied Magnetics reported a profit of $0.75 per diluted share in is fiscal third quarter ended June 30 versus a $0.10 per diluted share profit one year ago. Third quarter sales were $124 million versus $74 million last year.
